txt: (His voice echoes from downstairs.) "What the hell is going on up there?"
(His voice echoes from downstairs.) "What's going on up there?"
A competent work of taxidermy, the white and brown seabird lies among piles of coasters and drying mugs, one of its wings broken. The man is trying to mend it.
A man in his late twenties stands behind the counter, inspecting a stuffed seabird. As you approach, he gives you a sideways glance, then looks down again.
A man in his late twenties with a thin, unimpressive beard notices you approaching. He drops the ledger he was holding and turns to the lieutenant.
A rather lonely applause echoes through the mostly empty cafeteria. It's Garte. "Not bad," he tells you with an approving nod.
After a moment, he speaks. "Maybe you could send the shoes to him? In the hospital. Maybe it'd cheer him up. Do you know where he is?"

He blinks, as one might at a burning motor-carriage. "It is though. Right now, it literally *is* my business..."  He shakes his head -- and stops as a strange, new, cruel light rekindles in his features.
He crosses his arms: "Now. I still have to charge you for three nights and the broken window -- that's 100 square."
He demonstratively suppresses a world-weary sigh.
He doesn't say what's up with that.
He doesn't take the bait.
He glares at you suspiciously. "Well?"
He grimaces. "I think *fugue states* are more your *forte*, officer."
He ignores you.
He is very still as he watches you pocket the key.
He keeps his eyes on you, ignoring the boy.
He laughs. "What in the name of God..."
He looks at the dust on his finger and wipes it off.
He looks at you spinning your arms, then leans on the corner and sighs. His head drops between the shoulders, heavy and defeated.
He looks at you with his head tilted and his brow furrowed: "Fine."
He looks down at the stuffed bird, quietly shaking his head.
He looks pained on your behalf.
He looks you in the eye. There is silence in the space between you.
He nods back at you -- even more stoically.
He nods. "Happy to help, officer."
He nods. "Yes. You know. And I went outside and took care of it. Everybody calmed down. Felt like the right thing to do."
He pauses, realizing the contradiction in his statement. "Evidence being money. You can't stay here without *money*."
He pretends not to hear you, concentrating on the bird instead.
He realizes something. "Does it mean you talked to her? What else did she say about me?"
He refuses to reply. Only his breathing quickens with badly-concealed irritation.
He rolls his eyes. "Anything else you need?"
He rolls his eyes. "He wasn't pan-fried. He was *lynched*. What could the kitchen *possibly* have to do with..." He changes his mind.
He rolls his eyes. "If you say so."
He rolls his eyes. "The Return of what? Some commie bullshit? The Return of the king? I don't concern myself with paranoid political rumours. I have a *real* place to run."
He rolls his eyes. "Then why are you wasting my time... and yours?"
He rolls his eyes. "Those machines are Whirling property. But, if it makes you *feel* any better, I'm *not* planning to sell them."
He rolls his eyes. "What *thing*?"
He rolls his eyes.
He scowls. "No. But we could... *diversify* the entertainment options. Seeing as you've opened the door back there... The machine we have in the corner now is broken."

He searches underneath the counter. After a moment, he produces a pair of neon sneakers, packaged in a plastic bag. A postage label directs it to the Whirling-in-Rags, to the 'Wildest Cop in Revachol'.
He shakes his head as he returns the key under the desk. "No. I don't feel bad enough to give you a refund. Now, is there anything else you want?"
He shakes his head. "There is no gaping maw. If you don't want to tell me you don't have to. It's okay."
He sighs so much he seems to deflate. He slams the key before you. "The room is yours for the night. Don't forget you'll need *another* 20 reál tomorrow."
He smiles ashamedly through the rebuke. He feels the sting for a moment before returning the key under the desk. "I understand. Is there anything else you want?"
He smiles. It's a moment before he puts the key back under the counter. "Anything else I can do for you, then?"
He stands silently looking at the coins on the counter.
He stands silently looking at the coppers on the counter.
He stares at the key before him on the counter, then up at you.
He stares at you in disbelief. "Sure. That's it then. You're not getting into the room. Sort your shit out elsewhere."
He stares at you, beady-eyed...
He stares at you. There is silence in the space between your bodies.
He startles. "What wall?"
He takes a bottle of wine off the shelf and pours himself a glass. "They ride the cock carousel until the clock runs out. Here. Have the rest." He corks the bottle and hands it to you.
He takes a breath, and says hurriedly, "I don't make the rules. Pay 20 reál or sleep in the trash container. It's not up to me."
He takes a breath. "I don't make the rules. Pay 20 reál or sleep in the trash container. I don't care which you do. The key is yours if you want it."
He takes out his key chain and fiddles with the mechanism behind the counter. "The electronic lock to your room has been disabled till 21.00 tomorrow."
He takes out his key chain and fiddles with the mechanism behind the counter. "The electronic lock to your room will remain disabled till 21.00 tomorrow."
He takes the key from the counter and puts it back under the counter. "Now, is there anything you wanted?"
He takes the keys from under the counter and hands them to you: "Just bring them back once you're done, please."
He turns to the lieutenant. "I'm sorry, but he has to pay, I can't let him stay here any longer if he doesn't. If he doesn't have the money by tonight, then..." He shrugs.
He turns to the lieutenant. "Is this what you get when you call the police now? We've been waiting for a week here!"
He wrinkles his nose. "Who told you that?"
His brow furrows in confusion. "You're expecting a package? To arrive for you here?"
His eyes flash with fury. "You want a free place to sleep? Fine."
His eyes go wide with recognition. "Oh my god, the package -- I forgot, yes, yes it did arrive, when you were..." He stops, unsure how to continue.
His face expresses profound doubt in your *having this*.
His face moves between a sympathetic smile and a sincere frown. Unsure what to do, he covers his mouth with his hand and pretends to cough.
Looks like the bird was ripped off the shield that was used to mount it -- most likely on a wall.
Seeing the disappointment in your face, he relents. "Oh, fine, hero-cop. Lena left a forwarding address. 1113 Tabernacle Road, in Jamrock. If you see them again... do give them my best."
The breath catches in his chest. The light in his eyes snuffs out all at once. After a moment, he speaks.
The man actually remains silent this time. He looks at you expectantly.
The man in the vest and the violet shirt stares at the tape you've just given him. He begins to frown. Hard.
The man leans his hands on the corner and sighs. His head drops between the shoulders, heavy and defeated.
The man plucks at the seabird, frowning.
The man stands silently behind the counter, with his eyes fixed on the broken taxidermy, then on the ledger. He does not know what to say anymore.
The man starts to say something, but then thinks better of it. "Good luck."
The man wants to say something, then thinks better of it. "Good luck."
Wordlessly, he places it back under the desk.

"'Defended' may be putting it a bit generously, though. I had a great view of you doing *nothing* to stop those psychopaths. Then I crawled inside. Bullets started flying. Anyway..." He clears his throat.
"*Callous*? What are you, Kras Mazov? Almost all establishments in Revachol keep their trash locked. The Whirling-in-Rags is not special in that regard."
"*Hail Holy Queen* by The Etenniers. 'Hail holy queen of the sea,'" he quotes. "'You're whirling in rags -- you're vast and you're sad."
"*I* don't place much stock in the curse and so on, but the label frightens the clientèle. Who wants to stay at a *doomed* hostel? Everything's doomed enough without that..."
"*You* broke the skua?!" His face is flushed with emotions. A rash covers his neck.
"...that really *sucked*."
"...what?"
"A lot of people got killed because some asshole wanted to sing karaoke."
"A lot. A lot-lot. For the room, drinks, and broken window -- 130 reál."
"A lot. For the drinks and broken window -- 70 reál."
"A lot. For the room and broken window -- 100 reál."
"Absolutely not. That would be idiotic. I have no idea why you're even saying this right now..."
"Absolutely not." He breathes in and out. "Fuck you for even implying it. It wasn't me, it wasn't my staff. The establishment will look at it and ascertain what it was."
"Absolutely out of the question."
"Ah, 'Smallest Church in Saint-Saëns,' right?" The cafeteria manager is waiting for you to acknowledge that he recognized the song.
"Ah, them! Nice people -- but no. Lena said they were going back to Jamrock. I saw them pass by, outside." He waves at the windows. "This was *before* the fight started."
"All the locks have an electronic component. They have to be unlocked down here -- with a *master* key before your *guest* key will open the lock."
"All yours." He hands it to you quickly. "Anything else?"
"Alright." He calms himself. "Did she say anything else? About me, you know." He repeats: "Did she say anything about *me*?"
"Also!" He wags his finger. "You and your partner are staying here *free* now. I'm not gonna let you ruin it for him. This establishment supports cops. Even cops like you."
"Always happy to have officers from the RCM as guests." He takes the money and hands him a keyring. "Anything else I can do for you?" He looks at the lieutenant, avoiding your gaze.
"Am I smiling? Do you see me smiling and shaking my little shaker? No? Do you know *why?*"
"Am I wearing a little bow tie? Am I wearing a bow tie and doing this?" He shakes the imaginary shaker, furiously.
"Am I? Or did you ride in, take the body down, solve the murder, and *not* trash my hostel room?"
"An omen?" He looks at you, his neck crooked and his brow furrowed, then says shakes his head: "Whatever..."
"And I don't like the dead body that's been hanging out there for a week!" He gestures somewhere outside. "No one wants to work in these conditions!"
"And for god's sake watch out for yourself."
"And want me to make an exception for you? You're not even a hostel guest till you pay your outstanding bills..." He changes his mind.
"And... I'm sorry about the other night. I'm sorry I told you to sleep in the trash. That was wrong of me."
"Another thing -- great. I love those."

"Another thing you've annihilated is half the bar -- you've run a tab of 30 reál. Actually more, but we'll round it down to 30 for your hard work maintaining the stability and order of Revachol. That's 60 + 40 + 30 = 130 reál. And yes, reál is still money."
"Anything *else* I can do for you, officer?"
"Anything else I can do for you, officers?" The man smiles at you both.
"Anything else I can do for you?"
"Anyway -- thank you for clearing it up. Now, if there isn't anything else..." He does not seem to be overjoyed about his new-found professionalism.
"Anyway, I can't help you there. A lot of women come and go here."
"Anyway, I thought we were talking about the Whirling."
"Anyway, I'll forward that woman her bill and be done with it... Now, was there anything else?"
"Are you kidding me?"
"Are you serious right now?"
"Are you serious? From your work, I don't know... you can take bribes, I guess." He looks at lieutenant. "I'm sorry. I don't think cops take bribes."
"Are you serious? From your work, I don't know... you can take bribes, I guess." He looks at the lieutenant. "I'm sorry. I don't think cops take bribes."
"Are you sure, ma'am?"
"Are you trying to frighten me now?" He turns to the lieutenant: "What is this?"
"As a matter of fact, I do." He looks behind a pile of coasters, finds a slip of paper, and hands it to the lieutenant.
"As a matter of fact, you already have the key to your new room -- the trash container, remember? You said you'd give the key back and didn't..."
"As a police officer, you must understand that I cannot take you at your word -- without *evidence*."
"As it should be. Anyway. Thank you for returning my key."
"Because I'm not a bartender. I'm a cafeteria manager. Is there anything else you wanted?"
"Because this is a *culinary* establishment, not a morgue. I can't believe you even asked me."
"Because you haven't taken it away yet, and it must be stinking *hard* about now. Well -- you're not putting it here. Rest assured."
"Behind this building, there's a courtyard." He points to the kitchen behind him. "They hoisted him up on a tree there."
"Besides, the RCM doesn't *do* search warrants. I know the law. You'll just have to wait for the kitchen to open -- if you *have* to get in there. Which you don't."
"But it's not inane, I just... you owe me money."
"But this establishment only takes cash. Now, do you have that cash, Mr. Novelty Cheque Man?"
"But uh, are you done now? Can I unplug the microphone? I'd like to unplug the microphone." He's ready for things to get back to normal.
"But you know what? You're in luck. Because you don't have to ever pay me again."
"By causing more trouble? I think we're good."
"By the way, if you hadn't paid before 21.00, your door would have been locked electronically." He taps his foot against a metal box installed in the back of the bar counter.
"Can I help you?" He arches an eyebrow.
"Capitalist *plot*." He rolls his eyes. "The pinball we have in the corner now is broken -- I want to diversify the entertainment options."
"Cool. Okay." He inspects the bird. "I was really hoping *not* to think about the cock carousel any longer, because it made me feel like *shit* -- but this *is* a competent piece of taxidermy."
"Cool." He really does sound like he thinks it's a little *cool*. "Now, what can I do for you?"
"Do I *look* like I'm laughing? Do you see a *smile* on my face? I know what this is about. This is about the electronic lock not letting you in your room -- and it's anything but *funny* to me."
"Do I have a shaker in my hand? Is this..." He points to his empty hand. "Is this a shaker?"
"Do I have to answer him?" He asks the lieutenant. "Is this mandatory?"
"Do you *have* money tonight?"

"Does she? Maybe she does... maybe she *pertains* to the apocalypse." He snorts. "Sylvie is not here because I asked for her number. The dead body out back didn't help either, but it was mostly me. I hope you appreciate that..."
"Does that arrangement include... you paying me *what we already agreed* you owe me?"
"Does this *look* like part of a *Doomed* Commercial Area?" He makes a sweeping gesture. "This pre-revolutionary tile work? These high ceilings? The nice rooms? Well, *most* of the rooms..."
"Don't be an imbecile, I'm not going to serve you a Marinella. I have work to do -- and broken things to fix -- if that was all, I'd like to return to it."
"Don't thank me yet. You still owe me 100 reál. If you don't have it by tonight, I can't let you up there..." He points upstairs, toward your room.
"Don't thank me yet. You still owe me 100 reál. If you don't have it by tonight, I just can't let you up there..." He points upstairs, toward your room.
"Don't thank me yet. You still owe me 60 reál for three nights stay. If you don't have it by tonight, I can't let you up there..." He points upstairs, toward your room.
"Don't thank me yet. You still owe me 60 reál for three nights stay. If you don't have it by tonight, I just can't let you up there..." He points upstairs, toward your room.
"Don't thank me. You still owe me 30 for the drinks! If you don't have it by tonight I'm not letting you back up there..." He points upstairs.
"Don't thank me. You still owe me 70. If you don't have it by tonight I'm not letting you back up there," he points upstairs.
"Especially when you're so busy doing *nothing* to stop psychopaths. How could you just stand there? Still, you did risk your life..."
"Even if it is part of the damn Doomed Commercial Area..."
"Even more reason for me not to serve you, sir. Was there anything else you needed -- other than alcohol?"
"Everyone *knows* of it."
"Extra fine."
"Fantastic."
"Fine -- fine! Finger-bang him then, I don't care." He snorts angrily, then turns back to his activities.
"Fine, I'll take it off the bill! Sleep in a post-apocalyptic hell-hole if you want to. Just know I won't give you another room."
"Fine, I'll take it off the bill! You want to sleep in a post-apocalyptic shit-hole, go ahead! But I'm not giving you another room."

"Fine, fuck this. I'll do it myself, I'll call your station... what was it, 41? I'll ask them to pay for the room. The drinks and the window you still have to pay for. That's 70. Are we done, officers?"
"Fine, okay. A little." He shrugs. "But my job doesn't leave me time for wondering about *one* locked door in *one* of the cafeterias I manage..."
"Fine, yeah, it looked like someone had messed with the wiring. It was shortly after the hanging, but I don't know if it's at all related... Plenty of assholes around here who aren't murderers."
"Fine. Fine. *After* you've paid your bills you can climb that stage and do whatever the hell you need to do. *After*." He shakes the tape at you. "Damn this karaoke machine..."
"Fine. Fine. Climb on that stage and do your thing, just get out of my hair." He shakes the tape at you. "I'll plug it in for you. Damn this karaoke machine..."
"Fine. Okay. The kitchen is closed until 13:00 because the cook is working. You can snoop around after that -- if you must."
"Fine. Was there something you wanted?"
"For 14 years, man -- that's how long I've worked here. I've kept this place up through hail and through sleet. Fuck me, if some Doom Ghost..." he steadies his voice.
"For god's sake, stop SHOUTING!" The man behind the counter shouts. "Stop breaking things in my establishment! Stop provoking those oafs!"
"For god's sake, stop SHOUTING!" The man behind the counter shouts. "Stop crashing into people in my establishment! Stop provoking those oafs!"

"For survival, to pay *me*. Unless you want to become a *hobo*? Do you want to become a hobo? There's nowhere else to stay in Martinaise and it's a cold spring outside. Money doesn't make you happy but it lets you be *un*happy for a bit longer."

"For survival, to pay *me*. Unless you want to become a *hobo*? Do you want to become a hobo? There's nowhere else to stay in Martinaise and it's a cold spring outside. Money doesn't make you happy but it lets you be *un*happy for a while longer."
"For the drinks -- 30 reál."
"For the room -- 60 reál."
"Forget it."
"Forgive me for saying this, but your colleague seems more committed to drinking and..." He stops mid-sentence.
"Fuck you, man."
"Fucker?" He shakes his head. "Lay off the swear words, they don't make you *cool*. This isn't kindergarten."
"Game? *Everything* is just a game to you, isn't it?"
"God... does it mean you talked to her? What else did she say about me?"
"God..." He does not look too pleased.
"Good for you. I'm not letting *anyone* up there again -- ever. Now what did you want?"
"Good for you. Was there something else? I'd like to get back to what I was doing."
"Good luck trying to use it." He taps his foot against a metal box installed in the back of the counter.
"Good luck."
"Good thing that guest pays for her stuff on time -- I'll forward her the bill and be done with it. Was there anything else?"
"Good, good," the cafeteria manager intervenes to cut the moment short. "Are we ready? I want to unplug the microphone now."
"Good. It's good you're sorry. I'm not letting *anyone* up there anymore. Now what did you want?"
"Good. You got the room for the night, but remember -- you'll need *another* 20 reál tomorrow."
"Got the 20 reál?"
"Great, perfect, I hope you enjoy your freezing cold room with the window you broke *yourself*."
"Great, thank you officer, that's *all* I wanted -- payment for services rendered. If you continue to stay here, I just ask that you please pay your nightly bill in advance, starting tomorrow."
"Great, thank you officer, that's *all* I wanted, payment for services rendered."
"Hah! I knew it. I've always wondered where those machines by the door came from -- *and* they told me there was some kind of pinball thing here too..."
"Hah! Well!" He comes up with a counterargument. "We don't have any tapes. They all got stolen."
"Happy to help, officer. Anything else I can help you with?" He puts the package back under the counter.
"Haven't you asked me that already? What is it with you and this woman? She has nothing to do with this. "
"Heh..." A mirthless laugh. "Cock carousel -- I think I understand now. It's what they ride. Until, like, 39."
"Here. A new room key." He places a key on the counter in front of him. "It's the key to the trash container outside."
"Hey." He nods in greeting. "Was there something you needed?"
"How can I forget about it?" He stops the slow clap. "It was *unforgettable*..."
"How... strange. *I* certainly didn't put them there."
"Huh?"
"I asked an employee out. She didn't want to come, but felt obliged to. It was a bad idea. Now what is so god damn fascinating about that for you? It's got nothing to do with the lynching."
"I can fix it to the plaque and have a... new bird in the establishment I guess?" He hesitates. "So, I don't know... thank you? I'm gonna go with *thank you*."
"I can't believe it... I was so sure it was Sylvie. Even worse, I thought she was trying to send me a *message*. Symbol of hope and all..."
"I could if I were a bartender. But I'm not, I'm the cafeteria manager. So I won't."
"I didn't." He turns to the lieutenant: "I don't appreciate this. What is this?"
"I don't care what you do. Sleep in the trash or pay for a room -- I don't care anymore."
"I don't care. You're not putting a dead body into my fridge."
"I don't know who killed him, I'm not the police. That's your job."
"I don't know. Am I?" He looks at you, taking stock of your cop-ness and finding it lacking.
"I don't really know. You'll have to ask her."
"I don't really need you to *say* anything, I just need the money."
"I don't really use words like that to describe my clients, and maybe you shouldn't either…" He purses his lips. "Seeing as you're a cop and all."
"I don't remember *everyone* who comes here." He shakes his head. "And -- many people wear sunglasses inside lately. Must be a fad."

"I don't. I'm simply providing a service -- or, really, facilitating the offering of services to *paying* customers, and..." He runs out of steam. "It doesn't matter. I don't have to explain myself to you."
"I get it. You were *purposefully* shit. So original. I'm not letting *anyone* up there again -- ever. Now what did you want?"

"I give credit where credit is due and that -- was crazy. To throw a petroleum bomb at him and then *miss*. Maybe not super effective, but very *crazy*. I was watching until that, then crawled inside. Bullets started flying. Anyway..." He clears his throat.

"I give credit where credit is due and that was a crazy move -- crazy *effective*. Petroleum bomb, never seen anything like that... I was there until it struck him, crawled inside then. Bullets started flying. Anyway..." He clears his throat.
"I give credit where credit is due and that, sir -- was a nice shot. I was watching until you hit him, crawled inside then. Bullets started flying. Anyway..." He clears his throat.
"I give credit where credit is due and that, sir -- was an honest effort. I was watching until it *went* down. Crawled inside then. Bullets started flying. Anyway..." He clears his throat.
"I have *no idea* what that means."
"I have *three* cafeterias I manage. Three. Get over it."
"I have no idea what you're talking about."
"I have three cafeterias to manage. *Three*. Sylvie tends the bar here, not me, I'm only standing in."

"I hope at least your partner is recovering quickly. Also!" He raises his finger. "You're staying here for free now. That's right, this establishment supports cops. The stay is free -- the drinks are not," he adds. "Just felt I needed to specify that."
"I hope at least your partner is recovering quickly. Also!" He wags his finger. "You're staying here for *free* now. That's right. This establishment supports cops. Even cops like you."
"I hope it is."
"I knew it." He repeats. "Were there any back there? In working order I mean?"
"I knew it."
"I mean no offence. It's really nothing personal. I just *have* to protect the interests of this establishment."
"I mean, you're a detective, perhaps you can track them down? Shouldn't be that hard..."
"I really don't know what to say to that." He looks down at the seabird.
"I see." It's clear he's disappointed. "Well, thank you for the intel anyway. Shame about the bird."
"I should have known -- it was her way of telling me to piss off. I should stuff it up my ass." He stops and stares at the counter.

"I should have known Sylvie wouldn't *accidentally* break things here..." He inspects the bird, somewhat suspiciously -- then mellows. "Okay. This is actually a nice bird. A competent piece of taxidermy."
"I vouch for my staff as I would for myself... and I certainly wasn't the one making holes in our walls." He folds his arms and glares at you defiantly.
"I was merely clearing up the difference. What did you want with it?"
"I was... just wondering." He appears to be making a calculation in his head. "If you found pinball machines there..."

"I wish you a quick recovery. Also!" He raises his finger. "You and your partner are staying here free now. This establishment supports cops. The stay is free -- the drinks are not," he adds. "Just felt I needed to specify that."
"I would suppose it's because they have nothing better to do."
"I'll call them for recompensation for the room. But you still owe me 70 for the drinks and the window. And I do *not* think women are mentally inferior to men."
"I'll have it fixed at once. Thank you for letting me know. I assure you -- the Whirling does *not* abide spying on its guests."
"I'll unlock the electronic lock to your room." He taps his foot against a metal box at the bar counter. "All the doors lock automatically at 21.00."
"I'll unlock the electronic lock to your room." He taps his foot against a metal box installed in the back of the bar counter. "All the doors lock automatically at 21.00."
"I'm glad she got out of here before all that. Bullets flying and stuff... people inside were quite terrified you know. I had to take action and step outside too..."
"I'm not a fishing-teacher." He spreads his hands. "That is not why we keep our trash locked. Any place with a kitchen does it, it's not *political*, I assure you."
"I'm not dignifying that with a response."
"I'm sorry, but I can't let him stay here if he doesn't pay... He's three days on the slip. If he doesn't have the money by tonight, he'll have to work this from home."
"I've been working here for a *long* time, and that intercom has *never* been used by the Whirling."
"If it's a personal matter, why in the name of god should I..." He stops mid-sentence. "Okay, whatever."
"If you do find out who cut the line, though, let me know so I can forward them the repair bill."
"If you had a warrant, you'd be shoving it in my face right now." He crosses his arms.
"If you run out of money, you die. It's like that for all of us -- me too. That's why I need you to pay me." He stops and says, mostly to himself: "I'm not an asshole."
"Is it? Because I thought you were supposed to be investigating the lynching, not my employer conduct."
"Is that so? Mr. Feminist..." He catches the rest before it leaves his mouth, probably thinking it's best not to say anything.
"Is there something I can do for you?"
"Isn't it a bit too late for that?"
"It does, doesn't it."
"It is, isn't it?" He looks at you, shaking his head in disbelief.
"It is." He stands silently looking at the coins on the counter.
"It is." He stands silently looking at the coppers on the counter.
"It was all right." He doesn't sound like he thinks you *rocked* it. "Subdued. I might start letting people up there again... Now, what can I do for you?"
"It wouldn't hurt to get a little life in here. Other than the hellish karaoke machine. That one's always *causing trouble*."
"It's a *sign* of the Whirling-in-Rags not being part of the Doomed Commercial Area. If anything -- we're *revitalizing* this neighbourhood."
"It's for the..." He begins confidently, but then stumbles on his own words. "It's for no one. It's a prop. I'm not letting anyone use it after the Great Karaoke Catastrophe of '44."
"It's good you paid before 21.00, or your door would have been locked electronically." He taps his foot against a metal box installed in the back of the bar counter.
"It's not *strange*, it's inconvenient."
"It's not for bands, it's for clients. *Some* clients, okay? Not you."
"It's you, it's obviously you. *You* smell like liquor. And you're orange."
